en: Itivuttaka 46 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Ānanda. The venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by me,' he did so because he intended to speak further on this very subject. Now, friends, let us go to the Blessed One and inquire about this matter. As we hear it from the Blessed One, so shall we remember it. "Yes, friend," those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Ānanda. Then the venerable Ānanda, together with a number of bhikkhus, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side. Sitting there, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by me,' he did so because he intended to speak further on this very subject. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would explain the meaning of these words. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will remember it. "Well then, Ānanda, listen and pay close attention; I will speak. "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: "Ānanda, when I said, 'This has been said by me,' I said it with reference to two things. What two? With reference to the body and with reference to the mind. Ānanda, if a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world, then for that bhikkhu, whatever evil unwholesome states have arisen in connection with the body, they do not remain; and whatever evil unwholesome states have not yet arisen, they do not arise in the future. If a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... If a bhikkhu dwells contemplating mind in mind... If a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world, then for that bhikkhu, whatever evil unwholesome states have arisen in connection with phenomena, they do not remain; and whatever evil unwholesome states have not yet arisen, they do not arise in the future. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. You should train yourselves thus: 'We will dwell contemplating feelings in feelings... We will dwell contemplating mind in mind... We will dwell contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. Indeed, Ānanda, if you dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world, then for you, whatever evil unwholesome states have arisen in connection with the body, they will not remain; and whatever evil unwholesome states have not yet arisen, they will not arise in the future. If you dwell contemplating feelings in feelings... If you dwell contemplating mind in mind... If you dwell contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world, then for you, whatever evil unwholesome states have arisen in connection with phenomena, they will not remain; and whatever evil unwholesome states have not yet arisen, they will not arise in the future. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has the Dhamma been explained by the Blessed One in many ways. Those who have faith in the Blessed One are well-fortuned; those who have taken refuge in the Blessed One are well-fortuned. For the Blessed One has made known the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and has revealed the holy life in its full perfection and purity. Having said this, the venerable Ānanda paid homage to the Blessed One and, keeping him on his right, departed. Then the Blessed One, soon after the venerable Ānanda had left, addressed the bhikkhus: "Bhikkhus, when Ānanda rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by the Blessed One,' he did so because he intended to speak further on this very subject. Now, bhikkhus, let us go to the venerable Ānanda and inquire about this matter. As we hear it from the venerable Ānanda, so shall we remember it. "Yes, venerable sir," those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a number of bhikkhus, went to the venerable Ānanda's dwelling, and after exchanging greetings with him, sat down at one side. Sitting there, the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda: "Ānanda, when you rose from your seat and entered your dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by the Blessed One,' you did so because you intended to speak further on this very subject. Now, Ānanda, explain the meaning of these words. As we hear it from you, so shall we remember it. "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the venerable Ānanda spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by me,' he did so because he intended to speak further on this very subject. Venerable sir, when I rose from my seat and entered my dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by the Blessed One,' I did so because I thought: 'The Blessed One has said this; now I must explain the meaning of these words to the Blessed One. As the Blessed One hears it from me, so will he understand it. "It is wonderful, Ānanda! It is marvelous, Ānanda! How well this has been stated by you. Indeed, Ānanda, when I rose from my seat and entered my dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by me,' I did so because I intended to speak further on this very subject. And when you rose from your seat and entered your dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by the Blessed One,' you did so because you intended to speak further on this very subject. Now, Ānanda, explain the meaning of these words. As we hear it from you, so shall we remember it. "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the venerable Ānanda spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by me,' he did so because he intended to speak further on this very subject. Venerable sir, when I rose from my seat and entered my dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by the Blessed One,' I did so because I thought: 'The Blessed One has said this; now I must explain the meaning of these words to the Blessed One. As the Blessed One hears it from me, so will he understand it. Venerable sir, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by me,' he did so because he intended to speak further on this very subject. And when I rose from my seat and entered my dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by the Blessed One,' I did so because I thought: 'The Blessed One has said this; now I must explain the meaning of these words to the Blessed One. As the Blessed One hears it from me, so will he understand it. Venerable sir, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, 'This has been said by me,' he did so because he intended to speak further on this very subject. The Discourse on the Benefits of Training.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; so I have heard:
"Monks, dwell with training as the benefit, with wisdom as the pinnacle, with liberation as the essence, and with mindfulness as the governing principle."

“Bhikkhus, for those who dwell with the training as their benefit, with wisdom as their supremacy, with liberation as their essence, and with mindfulness as their lord, one of two fruits may be expected:
either final knowledge in this very life, or, if there is a residue remaining, the state of a non-returner.
In this regard, it is said:
“One whose training is complete, who is not subject to falling away,
for whom wisdom is supreme, and who sees the destruction of birth— ”
That sage indeed, who bears his final body, has abandoned Māra and gone beyond old age; him I call a conqueror.
Therefore, always delighting in meditation and composed in mind, [one should strive].
“Exerting yourselves, seeing the end of birth,
O bhikkhus, having overcome Māra along with his army,
become those who have gone beyond birth and death.”
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
